prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: compact transparent four-stage rocket illustration for the Ferromark homepage.
Input image 1 is the current rocket edit target. Preserve its exact silhouette, upright orientation, proportions, FOUR body stages, bare metal fins, worn forged steel, realistic scratches, soft studio lighting, orange-hot engine glow, and genuine transparent background.

Change only the four labels on the body:
- Keep the upper stage word "COMMONMARK".
- Replace "GFM" with "GITHUB".
- Replace "FFM" with "FERRO".
- Keep the lower stage word "AFTERBURNER".
These four words are the only text. Render every word exactly, in bold condensed uppercase lettering, horizontally centered and fitted across its own stage.
Make all four labels clearly brighter and easier to read when the rocket is displayed at only 240–288 pixels high. Use broad pale silver metal letter faces with shallow engraved perimeters and dark bevel edges. The entire face of each letter must be light, rather than just a thin outline around a dark interior. Keep the letters physically part of the metal: engraved/inlaid brushed silver catching studio light, not flat floating graphic text. Give the lettering crisp contrast against the darkened steel beneath, while preserving the photorealistic metallic character. Increase the letter-face weight and usable word width enough to survive thumbnail scale.
Constraints: preserve every other part of the asset and keep it upright; the webpage will apply the requested 10-degree tilt. Fins remain completely unmarked. No extra text, no labels on wings, no "The Foundation", no extra stage, no background or cast-shadow plate, no graphic frame. Preserve native alpha transparency and the full object without clipping.
sourcePrompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: compact transparent illustration for the Ferromark homepage, matching the Ferramenta family icons.
Input image 1 is the Ferromark family icon. Transform its stamp subject into a miniature four-stage rocket while preserving its photorealistic product-icon treatment: forged blackened steel, worn bright edges, subtle tool marks, brushed metal, warm workshop character, crisp soft studio highlights, and orange-hot light as the only strong color.

Subject: one upright, compact, handcrafted metal rocket in a slight three-quarter front view from a little above. Its body consists of exactly FOUR distinct stacked stages from top to bottom:
1. CommonMark: the nose cone and upper body are one stage.
2. GFM: a short cylindrical middle stage.
3. FFM: a second short cylindrical middle stage.
4. Afterburner: the lower engine stage with a short orange-hot exhaust glow.
Three clear interlocking mechanical seams separate the four stages. Keep the seams subtle and physically plausible, like precision-fitted workshop parts. Two small metal stabilizer fins belong to the lower body and carry absolutely no writing. The four stage labels are the only text, each engraved into the front of its corresponding body stage, in restrained, legible condensed lettering: "COMMONMARK", "GFM", "FFM", "AFTERBURNER".
Composition: a simple, bold rocket silhouette, nearly vertical, fully visible, centered, with a tight but safe transparent margin. Designed to sit at about 280 pixels high beside a benefits list, so avoid tiny intricate accessories. Keep the rocket's proportions compact rather than very tall and slender. No separate pedestal or fifth stage.
Lighting/material: match the supplied icon closely; richly realistic tactile steel, bright worn edges, small scratches, subtle warm reflected light, dark smoked-metal tones. Orange light belongs only to the engine/exhaust. No glossy plastic or cartoon rendering.
Background: genuine transparent alpha, no room, no scenery, no wood backdrop, no painted checkerboard, no opaque cast-shadow plate.
Avoid: text on wings, "The Foundation", extra labels, banners, arrows, numbered callouts, UI, logos, watermark, vector styling, flat illustration, colored decorative panels, giant flames. Output only the isolated rocket asset.
treatment: Trimmed transparent margins, padded 20 pixels, resized to 864 pixels high, WebP quality 88 with lossless alpha. Display tilt is CSS.
